findings.title: Remove the second plateau from the gate-charge curve
findings.body: `mosfet.miller_plateau_timing` draws another flat segment from (625,85) to (650,85) on its VGS-versus-Qg graph. After VDS slewing finishes, finite gate capacitance requires dVGS/dQg > 0, not additional charge at constant VGS. This misrepresents the post-Miller interval as a second plateau outside the marked Qgd span. End the curve at (625,85), or retain a positive slope through its last point.

findings.title: Keep the closed-loop curve below the open-loop response
findings.body: In `opamps.dominant_pole_gain_bandwidth`, the curves cross near x=539; at x=630, closed-loop y=198 lies above open-loop y=205. This depicts closed-loop gain exceeding open-loop gain. The catalog's single-pole model requires |H| = A0/√((1+A0/N)²+(f/fp)²) < |A| = A0/√(1+(f/fp)²). Redraw the static curves using one illustrative A0, N and fp with shared log scales. Keep the closed-loop curve below the open-loop curve, approaching the same high-frequency asymptote; reposition the fcl guide accordingly.

findings.title: Keep the Butterworth attenuation slope increasing on the log axis
findings.body: The curve's downward slope rises to 32/30 between (220,116) and (250,148), then falls to 20/32 between (314,196) and (346,216). This contradicts the labeled logarithmic frequency axis and the catalog's Butterworth model. For z=(f/fc)^(2N), dA/dlog10(f)=20Nz/(1+z), which increases monotonically toward 20N. The sketch therefore incorrectly shows the attenuation slope easing after the knee, even as an illustrative response. Keep the early vertices and replace those after (190,91) with (220,113), (250,137), (283,166), (314,196), (337,219). This preserves both specification markers while restoring increasing slopes.
